sources.quote: need time and support from trusted caregivers to feel comfortable interacting in new places. ... Give notice about new people, events, and places. ... sources.quote: need time and support from trusted caregivers to feel comfortable interacting in new places. ... Give notice about new people, events, and places. ... Step by step, with time, you help your child adjust to this new place
sources.supports: Give notice and say what to expect, follow the child's lead and watch first, avoid labels, step by step. A page about shy or slow to warm up children, applied to being the birthday child at kindergarten.

sources.title: Helping Young Children Who Are Socially Anxious
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute (Katherine Martinelli, last reviewed July 1, 2026)
sources.quote: Go over where it will be, who will be there and what might happen. ... The effect of all this previewing and role playing is to make the activity feel less new and scary ... sources.title: Preparing Your Older Child for a New Baby: How to Help Siblings Adjust
sources.quote: Find chances to talk about baby. ... Explain that the baby will be cute but will also cry and take a lot of your time and attention. ... Read children's books about newborns and siblings with your child. ... Involve your preschooler in planning for baby. ... Plan a one-on-one date with your child. ... Time major changes in your child's routine. ... Expect your child to regress a little. ... Instead of telling them to act their age, let him have the attention they need.
sources.supports: Talk about the baby, say the baby will cry and take time, read books, involve the child, one on one dates, time big changes, expect a little regression.

sources.title: Preparing Your Child for a New Sibling
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute (Juliann Garey, last reviewed January 2, 2026)
sources.quote: The more time your child has to get used to the idea of a new baby, the better. ... Board books and picture books about new babies are a great thing to add to the usual bedtime ritual. ... Maybe they can help pick out clothes or books, or fix up the baby's room. ... get in some extra special alone time with each parent. ... older children also need to know things that will be difficult. ... Explain that you will be back with the new baby in a few days.
sources.supports: Time to get used to the idea, bedtime picture books, small jobs, alone time with each parent, and telling the child what will be hard and when the parent returns.

sources.quote: Find chances to talk about baby. ... Explain that the baby will be cute but will also cry and take a lot of your time and attention. ... Time major changes in your child's routine. ... Expect your child to regress a little. ... Instead of telling them to act their age, let him have the attention they need.

שנקרא ספרים על תינוקות במיטה,
ושנקבע דייט, רק שתינו.

ואני אשאל **שוב ושוב**, כל פעם מחדש.

לקחתי דקה כדי להבין.

sources.title: Preparing Your Older Child for a New Baby: How to Help Siblings Adjust
sources.quote: Find chances to talk about baby. ... Explain that the baby will be cute but will also cry and take a lot of your time and attention. ... Read children's books about newborns and siblings with your child. ... Involve your preschooler in planning for baby. ... Plan a one-on-one date with your child. ... Time major changes in your child's routine. ... Expect your child to regress a little. ... Instead of telling them to act their age, let him have the attention they need.
sources.supports: Talk about the baby, say the baby will cry and take time, read books, involve the child, one on one dates, time big changes, expect a little regression.

sources.title: Preparing Your Child for a New Sibling
sources.publisher: Child Mind Institute (Juliann Garey, last reviewed January 2, 2026)
sources.quote: The more time your child has to get used to the idea of a new baby, the better. ... Board books and picture books about new babies are a great thing to add to the usual bedtime ritual. ... Maybe they can help pick out clothes or books, or fix up the baby's room. ... get in some extra special alone time with each parent. ... older children also need to know things that will be difficult. ... Explain that you will be back with the new baby in a few days.
sources.supports: Time to get used to the idea, bedtime picture books, small jobs, alone time with each parent, and telling the child what will be hard and when the parent returns.
